designer.name: 4b - HubSpot: Update That Deal's Amount and Status

notes.content:
1 - CAPTURE LINE-ITEM PROPERTIES AND METAFIELDS

Your Custom Integration & Data Architecture, the sync and the mapping: Shopify's order webhooks feed Make directly, so the native integration's limits never apply. One Shopify call pulls every line-item property and metafield, which steps 4a, 5 and 8 map onto your Contact, Deal and Line Item properties. Engraving Text, Font and Gift Wrap stand in for your own line-item property names until you send the real list.

2 - NO DUPLICATE CONTACTS OR CORRUPTED DEALS

Your clean data handling: step 3 looks up the Shopify order ID before any deal is made, step 4a matches the contact on email, and shopify_order_id is set to unique values in HubSpot. If the native HubSpot app stays installed, its deal sync needs to be off, or orders can land as two deals.

3 - OPTIONS FOR YOUR EMAIL TOKENS AND ABANDONED CHECKOUT

Your Automated HubSpot Workflows & Personalization and Email Template Setup: the deal carries the order's options and the contact its last-order tokens and product image, which your post-purchase, upsell and re-engagement sequences and drag-and-drop templates pull in. Abandoned checkout runs as its own scenario on Shopify's checkout webhook, and only checkouts with an email that were never completed get through: the cart's options and recovery link land on the contact, so your abandoned cart sequence shows the options they picked, and a completed order clears the link. Step 6 sends the deal ID back to the order for the two-way sync.

4 - EVERY OPTION ON ITS LINE ITEM FOR REPORTING

Your Analytics & Custom Reporting: each line item keeps its own option and metafield values beside the deal's revenue and the contact's lifetime spend, the fields your dashboards group by for revenue, CLV and sales by product option variation. Line items with custom properties do this without HubSpot custom objects.
